notes: Compiled from 8+ YouTube video sources covering filmmaker/photographer location scouting frameworks and 100+ LA-specific geo-tagged filming locations. Boilerplate stripped. Real content: pragmatic scouting decision hierarchies, budget-tiered tactics, and a replicable location-verification pattern.

doctrine.core_operating_principle: Location scouting is a layered decision tree, not a checklist. Start with what you can access for free, verify current state before committing, and build a reusable geo-tagged database so every scout compounds future efficiency.

no_budget: Scout public property first: parks, street corners, underpasses, parking structures, rooftops with no gating
Use Google Earth + Street View as primary pre-scout tools before any in-person trip
Time visits to off-peak hours to avoid permitting triggers (early morning, weekday)
Frame selection can hide uncontrolled elements (backgrounds, signage) without cost
mid_budget: Negotiate with private property owners directly; offer credit, photos, or nominal fee
Use film-commission location databases (LA FilmLA, state commissions) to identify pre-permitted zones
Factor permit cost into location choice: some LA zones have flat-fee indie permits under $500
Scout weather windows and season match before booking to reduce re-shoot risk

location_finding_tactics: Atlas Obscura, Locationland (Robert Foulkes), and city-specific guide lists surface non-obvious architecture and lesser-known public spaces
Cross-reference multiple sources: IMDb filming locations + fan-documented frame matches + Google Earth coordinate pinning
Build facade match protocol: identify key architectural detail (window pattern, signage, corner geometry), find via Google Earth, confirm on Street View, then verify in person
Document changed elements (demolished buildings, new construction, repainted facades) with dated notes so the record remains accurate for future scouts
Use time-indexed frame verification: timestamp from original footage matched to current-state photo confirms viability

minimum_record_per_location: Visual landmark identifier (primary architectural feature that survives change)
Permit requirement flag + applicable permit category
Source film or project reference (for cross-validation)
geo_tagging_database_architecture.verification_workflow: Timestamp from source footage → identify visual landmark in frame → pull Google Earth/Street View at same coordinates → compare current state → flag delta (unchanged / modified / demolished) → log result with date

weather_and_season_strategy: Build a location database tagged by season viability: golden-hour angle by month, rain probability by quarter, vegetation state (bare vs. full canopy)
LA-specific: marine layer burns off by 10-11am June-August; schedule exterior shoots accordingly
Overcast days function as a free diffusion filter; flag locations where overcast improves the look vs. degrades it
negotiation_and_access_tactics: Lead with the project's visibility benefit to the owner, not the production's need
Offer deliverables the owner actually values: high-res photos of their property, social tag, screen credit
Set a walk-away threshold before entering negotiation; never reveal it
Verbal approval is not enough; get written confirmation (email acceptable) before scheduling crew

LA_specific_location_intelligence.source_films_documented: 8+ major films including Heat, To Live and Die in LA
LA_specific_location_intelligence.named_locations: 25+ specific LA locations geo-tagged with street addresses
top_public_access_categories: Rooftop access via commercial property negotiation (Downtown, Koreatown)
Public beach and port infrastructure (San Pedro, Long Beach)
Metro station architecture (some stations permit low-impact shoots without FilmLA)
LA_specific_location_intelligence.permit_notes: FilmLA is the primary permitting body. Certain zones classified as public ROW allow photography without permit; video production triggers different rules. Always check current FilmLA zone map before assuming public access.

doctrine.replicable_verification_pattern: Timestamp + visual landmark identifier + current Google Earth comparison = location verified. Apply to every candidate before committing crew time.
failure_modes_to_avoid: Scouting in person before completing remote pre-scout (Google Earth/Street View) wastes transit time
Assuming a location is accessible because it was used in a prior production; verify current access independently
Verbal-only permissions; always get written confirmation
Ignoring seasonal/weather viability until shoot day
Building a location list without access flags; inaccessible locations are noise
